title: "Cleanup deletions": finish a registered worktree whose .git file is already gone (plain-directory form plus guarded prune)
outcome: AGENTS.md "Cleanup deletions" names how a registered worktree whose `.git` file is already gone (an earlier non-forced removal stopped partway) is finished for a closed-item target: `git worktree remove --force` cannot (validate_worktree fails on the missing .git), so the plain-directory form `Remove-Item -LiteralPath <checked path> -Recurse -Force -Confirm:$false` applies to the checked path, followed by `git worktree prune` only when `git worktree prune --dry-run --verbose` names that worktree alone. Until then that case fails closed and goes to the coordinator.
acceptance: AGENTS.md "Cleanup deletions" states, for a closed-item registered worktree whose .git file is already gone, that the plain-directory forced form applies to the checked path followed by the dry-run-guarded `git worktree prune`, with wording concurred by both coordinators, sent to Greg and audited under CLAUDE.md's instruction-change conditions (a), (b) and (c).
The Markdown-only link check passes on the clean candidate commit and the review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding.
